text:
jordan: noticed a spike in GPU evictions in ap-southeast1 this morning, looks like tiny pods are scattering across racks and leaving 1-2 GPUs unusable per node. dashboard: https://redwood.internal/gpu/heatmap?range=6h

matt: saw that too, a lot of small inference pods with podAntiAffinity set are fragmenting racks. eviction rate up ~4x since 03:10 UTC

clare: infra-bot alert just fired for az ap-southeast1-b 03:12, network errors + kernel OOM on a few nodes? @jordan can you paste the pod list?

jordan: here, `kubectl get pods -n prod -o wide --selector=app=embedder` -> many on nodes gpu-shelf-03*, different racks. also saw `AttachVolume` delays in kubelet logs.

infra-bot: [ANOMALY] gpu-utilization imbalance across racks in ap-southeast1 detected. estimated stranded GPUs: 18. Recommend temporary packing override.

dan: are we seeing NIC flaps or just scheduler packing oddities? I grep'd `dmesg` on gpu-shelf-03-7 and saw `mlx5: event` spikes around 03:08

matt: mlx5 spikes usually means transient link errors which make nodes temporarily unschedulable -> scheduler backfills tiny pods elsewhere -> fragmentation. worth checking node readiness events.

aleena: I ran `kubectl describe node gpu-shelf-03-7` and there are repeated `NetworkUnavailable` and `KubeletNotReady` events for ~2m. pods evicted with reason: NodeAffinity/NetworkUnreachable.

jordan: ok so network blips are the root cause, but we still need short-term defrag because customers hit latency SLOs. proposal: run descheduler job targeting tiny pods (<0.5 GPU) to coalesce on healthy racks and then cordon+drain the flaky nodes. thoughts?

clare: +1. we should also avoid causing a larger churn during peak. plan: ramp descheduler with `maxPodEvictionsPerNode=1` and `evictionTimeBudget=5m`, monitor p95 latency.

matt: can do, I'll push a descheduler job in canary mode to ap-southeast1a first. command I used before:
```
kubectl apply -f descheduler-canary.yaml -n kube-system
# descheduler config has priorityThreshold and podSelector for tiny gpu pods
```

jordan: while that runs, I'll tag the flaky nodes with `maintenance:investigate` and create a quick autoscale override to reduce new tiny pod placement in ap-southeast1-b for 30m.

dan: also recommend enabling `TopologySpreadConstraint` fallback for the embedder service to prefer packing into fewer nodes when network flakiness is detected. low-risk change.

aleena: I'm seeing memory pressure on the warmpool nodes after initial descheduler evictions — p95 cpu spike on embedder groups. dropped replica from 12->10 temporarily to stabilize.

matt: canary descheduler ran: evicted ~27 tiny pods, consolidated onto 9 nodes, freed 11 GPUs in two racks. p95 latency unchanged so far.

clare: good. next step: cordon the top 4 nodes with repeated NIC events and drain after graceful pod relocation finishes. will open a runbook PR for the cordon/drain sequence.

jordan: opening incident note for tracking: INC-2026-0343, summary + links, assign to eng-platform oncall.

infra-bot: incident INC-2026-0343 created by jordan at 03:45 UTC. severity: sev2.

dan: FYI cost hit: consolidation increased burst on a few nodes, estimated hourly GPU cost delta +$18 for the interval, still cheaper than sustained latency penalties.

matt: drained 3/4 cordoned nodes, last one draining now. no restart storms. kube-scheduler logs show less evictions after 03:58.

clare: leaving notes for postmortem: root cause network NIC firmware regression + scheduler reactivity to transient NodeNotReady. mitigation ideas: firmware roll, softer backoff for scheduler requeue, and a targeted packing policy for tiny pods.

aleena: I'll keep monitoring for the next 6 hours and post a metric snapshot at +1h.

jordan: thanks all. action items: matt -> run descheduler canary + cleanup, clare -> PR runbook & postmortem skeleton, dan -> cost delta in incident, aleena -> metric snapshots, jordan -> coordinate firmware ticket with infra-hardware.

matt: noted. starting cleanup and will post command outputs shortly.

aleena: metric snapshot: https://redwood.internal/metrics/ap-southeast1/gpu-evictions?from=03:00&to=04:30

jordan: closing thread for now, reopen if evictions climb again. :thumbsup:
